promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Care for others and the community

questions.q: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, who stopped to help the injured man by the roadside?
questions.explain: Jesus taught that it was the despised Samaritan, not the religious officials, who showed true compassion.

questions.q: In which Gospel is the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats found?
questions.explain: The Parable of the Sheep and the Goats appears in Matthew chapter 25.

questions.q: Which Greek word describes the selfless, unconditional Christian love that inspires charity?
questions.explain: Agape is the selfless, self-giving love that Christians are called to show to all people.

questions.q: Jesus' teaching 'Do to others as you would have them do to you' is commonly known as the:
questions.explain: This teaching from the Sermon on the Mount is traditionally called the Golden Rule.

questions.q: Which Christian organisation, known for its social work with the poor, was founded by William Booth in 1865?
questions.explain: William Booth founded The Salvation Army in London in 1865 to help the poor and destitute.

questions.q: What does the Christian charity CAFOD stand for?
questions.explain: CAFOD is the Catholic Agency for Overseas Development, the official aid agency of the Catholic Church in England and Wales.

questions.q: Which UK Christian charity is best known for running a nationwide network of food banks?
questions.explain: The Trussell Trust supports a large network of food banks across the UK, rooted in Christian values.

questions.q: Complete this teaching from the Letter of James: 'Faith without works is ___.'
questions.explain: James teaches that genuine faith must be shown through actions such as caring for others.

questions.q: What is the main teaching of the Parable of the Good Samaritan?
options: Christians should only help other Christians
Christians should show love and compassion to everyone, including strangers
Wealth is a sign of God's favour
questions.explain: The parable teaches that a person's 'neighbour' is anyone in need, regardless of background.

questions.q: According to the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats, on what basis are people judged?
options: How they treated those in need, such as the hungry and imprisoned
The number of laws they kept
questions.explain: Jesus says 'whatever you did for the least of these' was done for him, linking judgement to practical care.

questions.q: What does the commandment 'Love your neighbour as yourself' teach Christians about social action?
options: They should treat others' welfare as importantly as their own
They should only care for their own family
They should love themselves before others
They should avoid contact with non-believers
questions.explain: This teaching calls Christians to actively care for the wellbeing of all people.

questions.q: Why do many Christians support charities such as Christian Aid?
options: Because helping the poor puts their faith into action
Because charity guarantees wealth in this life
questions.explain: Supporting charity work is seen as living out Jesus' teaching to serve those in need.

questions.q: What does Christian 'stewardship' mean in the context of social responsibility?
options: The duty to care responsibly for God's creation and resources
The rule that only priests may lead worship
The belief that the world will soon end
The practice of giving up all possessions
questions.explain: Stewardship teaches that humans are caretakers of the world God has entrusted to them.

questions.q: How did Zacchaeus show repentance and a concern for justice after meeting Jesus?
options: He gave to the poor and repaid those he had cheated
He became a priest in the temple
He refused to pay any taxes
He gave his family all his money
questions.explain: Zacchaeus gave half his goods to the poor and repaid fourfold anyone he had defrauded, showing restored justice.

questions.q: What does the Beatitude 'Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness' encourage?
options: A strong desire for justice and right relationships
A focus on gaining personal wealth
Fasting from all food and drink
questions.explain: This Beatitude praises those who long for justice and what is morally right.

questions.q: How does the belief that humans are made 'in the image of God' influence Christian attitudes to others?
options: It means every person has equal value and dignity
It means only Christians have worth
It means people should not be helped
It means wealth reflects God's approval
questions.explain: Being made in God's image gives all people equal worth, motivating care and respect for everyone.

questions.q: A Christian regularly volunteers at a shelter for homeless people. Which teaching best supports this action?
options: 'Whatever you did for the least of these, you did for me'
'An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth'
questions.explain: The Sheep and the Goats teaches that serving those in need is serving Christ himself.

questions.q: A wealthy Christian decides to donate a large part of their income to famine relief. Which teaching of Jesus most closely inspires this?
options: Jesus telling the rich young man to sell his possessions and give to the poor
Jesus calming the storm on the lake
questions.explain: Jesus challenged the rich young man to give to the poor, encouraging generosity over attachment to wealth.

questions.q: A church wants to help local families who cannot afford food. Which Christian charity would it most likely partner with?
questions.explain: The Trussell Trust runs food banks and often works with local churches to help those in food poverty.

questions.q: A Christian campaigns for fair trade so that farmers in poorer countries receive a just price. Which Christian principle does this best reflect?
options: Justice for the poor and oppressed
questions.explain: Campaigning for fair trade reflects the Christian call to justice, championed by charities such as Christian Aid.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Christianity: Religion & Social Action
